html:
President Trump is meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi today in Shenzhen for a historic three-way summit on the sidelines of APEC. This unprecedented gathering sees Chinese President Xi personally greeting President Trump on the tarmac, reciprocating a past gesture and underscoring China's perceived diplomatic centrality, even as the leaders come with differing priorities on trade, Ukraine, Iran, and arms control.

US Politics & Diplomacy: Domestically, Democrats have nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House, positioning him to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber when the party takes control in January following a sweeping midterm election triumph. In other US political news, defense secretary Pete Hegseth visited Venezuela, highlighting the capture of Nicolás Maduro by US special forces as a sign of US dominance and an improbable rapprochement. Meanwhile, the FAA administrator Bryan Bedford has taken responsibility for a recent nationwide flight stoppage, urging critics to "lay off" transportation secretary Sean Duffy.

Middle East Security: Tensions in the Middle East have escalated with tit-for-tat strikes between the US and Iran. The US military struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island, described by a US official as a self-defense action in response to Revolutionary Guard Corps aggression. In response, Iran claims its drones targeted US Patriot defense systems and launch platforms at the Ali Al Salem base in Kuwait, and explosions were reported at US bases in Bahrain as Kuwait repelled drone attacks. Additionally, three oil tankers reportedly caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, with one ADNOC vessel reporting one missing and eleven injured. Concerns also persist regarding reports of a possible Iranian "dirty bomb" plot in Washington, a matter President Trump is taking seriously despite some officials dismissing imminent threats. Amid this, a US aircraft carrier, the George Washington, has reportedly departed the Gulf region. In Gaza, the Israeli military launched a rare ground operation beyond the Yellow Line to dismantle a "terror tunnel," condemned by Hamas as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation and resulting in multiple fatalities. This incursion occurs as an Israeli parliament elects a speaker backed by opponents of caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Russia-Ukraine Conflict: The war in Ukraine continues, with a new video emerging showing explosions moments before a section of the Crimea Bridge collapsed, an infrastructure project Ukraine repeatedly targets. Elsewhere, Ukrainian forces are engaging Russian troops in an underground war within an old Soviet tunnel in the Kharkiv region, a frontline where "drones don't fly." Prince Harry, after a trip to Ukraine, warned on the threat from Russia, indicating he would rejoin the military if needed. Russian President Vladimir Putin used the APEC summit to promote Russia’s economy, suggesting the EU is losing industry and falling behind competitors, even as Ukraine's actions contribute to a fuel crisis in Russia.

Global Economy & Technology: The artificial intelligence sector is seeing major movements, with Anthropic setting its share price at $83 for its stock market debut, positioning it for one of history's biggest IPOs. Concurrently, Nvidia's board stated it would not reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang, despite pressure, following revelations related to a Chinese national and alleged sanctions skirting. In other tech news, Waymo has pulled its driverless taxis from freeways across the US after California banned the autonomous vehicles from its highways following recent traffic incidents. Iraq has also resumed shipping oil for export to Turkey via pipeline after a 12-year hiatus.

Human Rights & Social Issues: A UN committee adopted draft resolutions on Palestinian aid, property rights, and Israeli occupation, while the UK and Australia sanctioned Israeli firms involved in West Bank settlement building. The International Court of Justice is set to rule on a Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar, raising fears of potential US sanctions against a Nobel-winning judge. In the UK, a member of the anti-migrant group Raise the Colours was found guilty of murder, and the group faces a temporary ban on placing flags on public street furniture. El Salvador's model of mega-prisons to combat organized crime is garnering attention, with its president celebrating an attack on a key Haitian gang leader's home, as Salvadoran troops engage gangs in Haiti.
